title: Adaptive-routing degradation: root cause analysis, synthetic canaries, and hardening plan
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: During a regional capacity surge on 2026-02-23 we observed a sustained p99/p95 latency increase and a ~12% throughput drop for long-context text-generation requests. The immediate trigger was a scheduler change (autopreempt microbatching) combined with a tightened attention-autotile heuristic. The combination caused deterministic inputs to be routed to a less optimal kernel variant for long sequences, producing tail latency regressions under mixed-quant workloads. This ticket captures the root-cause analysis, telemetry findings, approved mitigations, and prioritized action items to prevent recurrence.
investigation_notes: Timeline: 2026-02-23 14:32 UTC first alert (p95 up 18%, p99 up 42%). On-call replicated increased long-tail latency with a synthetic repro workload by 15:10 UTC.

What changed: A low-risk scheduler change (RFC #497: microbatch preemption) was merged into runtime-1.19 on 2026-02-20 to improve fairness during bursty arrivals. Separately, an attention autotile threshold tweak (PR #611) reduced the size threshold which caused a different attention kernel to be selected for sequences >1024 tokens when quantized layers were present.

How they interact: The preemption behavior increases worker churn for microbatches serving long sequences, which amplified sensitivity in the kernel selector's cost model. The selector's cost estimate, which assumes steady microbatch occupancy, made a different choice (deprioritized fused-attn kernel) when the observed microbatch size and KV cache hit ratios diverged from historical averages.

Key symptoms: increased per-token scheduling jitter, spikes in context-switches in the serving worker, and a higher incidence of fallback execution paths during kernel warmup. Reproduced locally with a mixed-quant model (int8 for most layers, fp16 for prefix layers) and an arrival pattern of 30 concurrent long sequences with Poisson inter-arrival times.

Telemetry gaps discovered: No single signal captured the correlation between microbatch preemption events and kernel-selection flips. We lacked an end-to-end trace that ties scheduler preemption events, kernel choice, and per-token latency together in one view.

Customer-visible impact: A subset of customers using long-context endpoints saw occasional completions exceed SLO for p99, and a small number observed degraded throughput leading to transient rate-limited errors downstream in their apps.

Risk analysis: Reverting the scheduler change would reduce fairness gains for bursty traffic; reverting autotile heuristic would increase compute for some short-sequence users. Our mitigation strategy aims to be surgical: stabilize kernel selection without losing the scheduler improvements.
telemetry_findings: Metric correlations: p99 latency correlates with (1) increased microbatch preemption events per minute, and (2) the fraction of requests that triggered the smaller autotile kernel selection. Cross-correlation peak at ~2s lag.
Trace examples: Captured traces show preemption -> kernel probe -> warmup fallback -> elevated token latency for ~8-12 tokens. Average extra latency per affected request ~47ms at p99.
Distribution: Effect concentrated on requests with sequence length 1024-2048, using quantized model variants, at concurrency >24 per worker.
Alerting gaps: No dedicated alert for kernel-selector flip-rate or microbatch-preempt-rate. Existing SLO alerts signaled only after customer-visible SLO breach.

Benchmarks: Synthetic bench reproduces 10-15% throughput drop and similar p99 increase. Local microbench reveal kernel-choice boundary is unexpectedly sensitive to observed microbatch occupancy under preemption.
Repro instructions included: link to repro harness and runner parameters in links below.
decision_log: 2026-02-26: Short-term mitigation approved: add a conservative gating flag to the autotile heuristic to prefer the fused-attn kernel when observed microbatch churn is high. (Owners: Luis Alvarez & Jon Park)
2026-03-02: Do not revert microbatch preemption globally; decision to instrument and harden kernel scorer instead so scheduler benefits remain. (Approved by Eng Leads)
2026-03-05: Add synthetic canary job in CI and a production canary pipeline that injects controlled long-context traffic into a small subset of workers. (Owner: Jon Park)

2026-03-08: Implement deterministic fallback: if kernel scoring confidence < threshold and observed variance in microbatch occupancy > X, pin to historically stable kernel for the model-version. This will be toggled via runtime feature flag. (Owner: Sasha Ivanov)
2026-03-09: Prioritize telemetry unification so operators can trace scheduler preemption -> kernel selection -> token latency chain. (Owner: Anika Patel)
Rollout plan: Canary for 24h -> ramp to 10% -> 50% -> full if no regression signals. Each ramp gated by synthetic canary passing and no SLO regressions on production traces.

[A6] Post-deploy verification checklist for future scheduler/autotile changes (telemetry smoke, synthetic canary pass, 12h canary run). Owner: Engineering Leads. Due: 2026-03-18
